item.description:

item.description:

Analysts are closely watching Oracle's upcoming fiscal Q1 2027 report for signs of accelerated gigawatt delivery and improved cash flow to determine if its backlog will be an asset or a burden.

item.title: [AAPL Bearish (-0.26)] Hackers Are Exploiting a Mac Screen Sharing Flaw. Apple Says These 3 Updates Fix It

item.title: [MSFT Bearish (-0.32)] The rise of token-theft attacks: No password or MFA needed
item.description:
Sentiment: MSFT Bearish (-0.32)
Token-theft attacks are on the rise, allowing malicious actors to bypass passwords and multi-factor authentication (MFA) to access systems like Microsoft 365. Attackers achieve this by stealing session tokens or encrypted keys, often through methods like malware, adversary-in-the-middle phishing, malicious browser extensions, live-session abuse, or social engineering. Defending against these attacks requires a multi-layered approach, including implementing zero-trust strategies, user awareness training, auditing browser extensions, and establishing clear identity verification protocols for help desks.

item.title: [TSM Neutral (+0.02)] TSMC vs. ASML: Which Semi Monopoly Has the Wider Moat?
item.description:

While both are essential, the author argues that TSMC possesses a wider moat due to its sheer scale, operational efficiency, capital barriers, and a broad customer base that extends beyond AI chips, making it a more robust investment than ASML. The author also suggests that as the AI revolution evolves, investors should favor these monopolistic firms over commoditized chip makers, given the increasing capital expenditures and potential cost-cutting by hyperscalers.
